name: Registration

subjectOf.text: Freedom from supervision and disclosure obligations was functional rather than incidental for hedge funds: it enabled successful fund launches, helped generate higher returns, and attracted investors, which is why manager registration is contested.
subjectOf.abstract: Hedge funds' ability to invest in global markets without supervision and significant disclosure obligations was important for successful hedge fund launches, helped generate higher returns, and attracted investors.

scope_conditions: hedge funds operating before the Dodd-Frank Act
funds investing in global markets

subjectOf.text: The immediate deregistration of hedge fund advisers following Goldstein v. SEC is revealed-preference evidence of the industry's opposition to registration and disclosure requirements, not merely a technical response to the vacatur.

SEC as an instance of arbitrary rulemaking, because the SEC had no authority to define a term the Advisers Act left undefined.

subjectOf.text: This Article reports the first survey study of hedge fund advisers conducted after the SEC's registration effective date, drawing on a population of 1267 private fund advisers who registered before March 30, 2012.

subjectOf.text: Hedge fund adviser registration under the Dodd-Frank Act positively affects adviser returns in March 2012, but the effect does not persist in the months after the registration effective date.
